title: Status row (as a writer posts it)
description: One row per check, job, backup, service, VM, machine, link, grant or repo (plan.md 'Status: one screen for the whole fleet'). Writers POST rows to aico-web on loopback (POST /api/status/rows, one row or an array). The server stamps updated_at and works out the shown state: a row past next_run is 'late' (since next_run); rows of a machine whose own kind=machine row is late or off, or that has no kind=machine row, are 'unknown'. Readers (GET /api/status) get each row back with updated_at, shown and shown_since. Every validator (packages/status, native/host-steward/aico_status.py) tests against this file and contracts/status-row-fixtures.json.

id.description: Stable key the writer chooses, unique across the fleet: start it with the machine, e.g. 'davion-sidarli/notes-export'. Posting the same id again replaces the row.

what.description: What it is, in a few plain words ('Notes export to Drive').

kind.description: machine is the host's own row (next_run required): the unknown rule reads it.

machine.description: The host it runs on or is about: its short host name, lower case ('davion-sidarli'), the same id on every row from that host.

project.description: Project slug, when it belongs to one.

state.description: What the writer last saw. off: stopped or paused on purpose (never late, not a problem). late and unknown are never written; the reader derives them.

meaning.description: What the state means, in plain words ('Copied 412 notes to Drive.').

last_run.description: When it last ran or was last checked (RFC 3339).

next_run.description: When the next report is due (RFC 3339), slack included. Past it the row shows 'late since' this time. Leave it out for rows with no schedule; a kind=machine row must have it. Writers stamp it from their own clock: every host runs NTP and the slack covers what skew is left.

actions.description: What a person or agent can do about it, as data; the screen and CLI decide how to offer each. run: the command that runs it now. log: the command or path that shows its log; a command should print its last lines and end (for journalctl, -n 200 --no-pager), since Aico stops it after 10 seconds and shows what it printed by then as cut off. detail: an Aico app path with more. look: where a session looking into it should start (a path, project or hint). session: the id of a session the row is about; the screen offers Resume when Aico holds it after a crash, else Open.

owner_only.description: Only the owner can act or decide. A failed row raises an owner ask only when an action explicitly sets this to true.
